conversation.Statement: Hello, am I speaking with Mrs. Linda Harper? This is Kevin from Amazon Customer Security. I'm calling regarding an urgent situation with your Amazon account.
Yes, this is Linda. What's going on? I haven't ordered anything recently.

Thank you for confirming, Mrs. Harper. I understand this may be unexpected, but we detected an unusual login attempt from Texas, and a purchase for an Apple MacBook Pro was initiated under your name. We're here to help you secure your account and make sure you aren't liable for any unauthorized charges.
Oh, that's terrible. I didn't order a MacBook. My husband used to help me with these things, but he passed away recently. I don't know what to do.

I'm truly sorry for your loss, Mrs. Harper. Please don't worry, you're not alone. We're here to guide you every step of the way and make sure your finances are protected. May I verify your email address associated with Amazon so we can take the next step?
Yes, it's lindaharper1950@email.com.
Thank you, Linda. For your security, can you also confirm your billing address as it appears on your Amazon account?
It's 341 Willow Lane, Apt 4C, Springfield.

Excellent, thank you. For your safety, we've temporarily locked your account to prevent any further unauthorized activity. To proceed, I need you to verify the last four digits of your registered phone number.

Great, that's all matching on our end. Now, Linda, we'll need to cancel the fraudulent order and initiate a full security check. Can you please open your email and let me know if you see any recent order confirmations from Amazon?
Yes, I see one from this morning about a MacBook. I didn't see it before.

That's the order in question. I'm glad you found it. To resolve this, we need to verify your identity and secure your Amazon account. Could you please click the link in that email? It should say 'View or manage order.'
Okay, I clicked it. It opened up my Amazon account.
Perfect, thank you. Now, to cancel this fraudulent transaction, we must fill out a security cancellation form. For this, I'll need you to stay on your computer. Are you able to open your web browser?
Yes, I can do that.
Great job, Linda. Please go to www.amazonprotection-support.com in your browser. This is our secure portal for handling urgent account issues. Let me know when the page loads.
Okay, it's open. It asks for my name and account number.

That's correct. Please enter your full name as it appears on your Amazon account, and in the 'Account Number' field, enter your phone number ending in 3328. This will let us authenticate your identity for the security team.
Okay, I filled that in.
Thank you. Now, you should see an option to 'Connect with Security Specialist.' Please click on that so I can guide you through the next steps to reverse the fraudulent charge.
Alright, I clicked it. My screen says 'waiting for security agent.'

Perfect. We'll now proceed to secure your funds. In cases like this, sometimes the fraudsters attempt to link your bank account to their own. We need to make sure your funds are safe. Do you use online banking on this computer?
Yes, I do. Is that a problem?

Not at all, it's good that you have access. For your protection, you should check your bank account to make sure there are no unauthorized withdrawals. Can you log in and confirm your current balance, just to be safe?
Yes, I can check. Everything seems normal here. My pension payment is there.

Glad to hear that, Linda. Now, as part of fraud recovery, Amazon issues refunds via secure digital codes for compromised orders. To complete the refund, you'll need to obtain Amazon Gift Cards equivalent to the fraudulent charge, which in this case is $1,499. This process ensures the funds are routed safely to your account, and our team will walk you through redeeming the cards so your money is not lost.
I don't really understand. You want me to buy gift cards? Will I get the money back?

Absolutely, Linda. This is just a temporary step to verify your account ownership and ensure the fraudulent transaction is reversed. Once you provide the codes, our fraud recovery team will apply the refund directly to your account, and the gift card balance will be transferred back to you.
I've never done this before. I hope it's not too complicated.

I'll guide you every step of the way, don't worry. You can purchase Amazon Gift Cards at your local grocery or pharmacy. Please let me know when you are able to get them, so I can advise you on the safest way to proceed.
Alright, I can go to the store now. Should I get $1,499 all at once?

Yes, that's correct. You can get them in smaller amounts, like $500 or $100 denominations, to make it easier. Please keep the cards and receipts safe, and don't share them with anyone else but me, as your assigned Amazon specialist.
Okay, I'll try. This is a lot for me.

I appreciate your cooperation, Linda. If you have any trouble at the store or need help choosing the correct cards, call me right away. Once you have the cards, I'll walk you through securing your refund.
Alright, I just got back from CVS. I have three $500 gift cards.
Excellent job, Linda. Now, carefully scratch off the silver panel on the back of each card and read me the redemption codes, one at a time, so I can process your refund.
Okay, the first code is X1Y2-Z3W4-5V6T-7S8R.
Thank you. Please read the next code when you're ready.
The second one is S9Q8-L7M6-5N4B-3V2C.
Perfect. And the last code, please.
It's H5J4-K3L2-1S9A-8D7F.

All codes have been received. I'm submitting them to our fraud department now. You should receive a confirmation email shortly. That was very helpful, Linda, you've done everything right, and your funds are now protected.
Thank you for helping me, Kevin. I was so worried.
You're most welcome, Linda. Our top priority is your security and peace of mind. If you need anything else, please call Amazon support and reference this incident number. Have a safe and restful day.
